summary: Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi announced his resignation, with Major General Mykhailo Drapatyy appointed as successor. Russian sources report continued attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure including ports, logistics centers, and drone strikes across multiple regions. The US Senate will not release $400 million in military aid to Ukraine until fiscal year 2029.
key_points: Oleksandr Syrskyi officially announced his resignation as Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, stating he will serve Ukraine until victory. (Source: @UkraineNow/82825)
Mykhailo Drapatyy was appointed as the new Commander-in-Chief of the Ukrainian Armed Forces following Syrskyi's resignation. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31836)
Major General Igor Skibiuk will become the new Chief of the General Staff of the Ukrainian Armed Forces, replacing Andriy Gnatov. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31830)
Drone attacks hit logistics centers of Wildberries in Krasnodar and Stavropol regions, as well as an oil base in Armavir where a large-scale fire occurred. (Source: @UkraineNow/82826)

Russian forces conducted strikes on Ukrainian ports, maritime vessels, and logistics centers involved in the Armed Forces of Ukraine, according to the Ministry of Defense. (Source: @tass_agency/386534)

Maersk announced suspension of operations with one of Ukraine's largest ports due to risks, redirecting a ship with imports destined for the port of Chernomorsk to the Romanian port of Constanta. (Source: @tass_agency/386531)
The US Senate will not transfer $400 million in additional military aid to Ukraine approved by Congress, with funds only available in fiscal year 2029. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31820)

sections.executive_summary: Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi announced his resignation, with Major General Mykhailo Drapatyy appointed as successor. Russian forces continued attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure including ports, logistics centers, and drone strikes across multiple regions. The US Senate announced it will not release $400 million in military aid to Ukraine until fiscal year 2029.

points: Oleksandr Syrskyi officially announced his resignation as Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, stating 'My work is war. Positions change, but this principle does not.' He emphasized that under his command, 700 square kilometers of Ukrainian territory were liberated this year. (Source: @UkraineNow/82825)

Mykhailo Drapatyy was appointed as the new Commander-in-Chief of the Ukrainian Armed Forces, thanking President Zelensky for trust and emphasizing his commitment to defending the state. Drapatyy is a major general and holds the Order of Bohdan Khmelnytsky and the Order of the War Hero. (Source: @UkraineNow/82828)

Major General Igor Skibiuk will become the new Chief of the General Staff of the Ukrainian Armed Forces, with President Zelensky describing him as a very experienced military commander who has defended Ukraine alongside the new Commander-in-Chief. (Source: @UkraineNow/82833)

Drone attacks hit logistics centers of Wildberries in Krasnodar and Stavropol regions, as well as an oil base in Armavir where a large-scale fire occurred. These logistics centers are used for supplying components for drones, military navigation devices, and other dual-purpose goods for the Russian army. (Source: @UkraineNow/82826)
A drone strike on an fuel station in Kharkiv damaged a fuel distribution column, resulting in five casualties, all of whom were fuel station employees. (Source: @UkraineNow/82837)

President Zelensky discussed questions of resolving the situation in Ukraine with Witkoff and Shubernin, according to Axios, discussing ideas on how to resume diplomatic efforts to end the war. (Source: @tass_agency/386548)

President Zelensky stated that only Putin is the cause of the war starting and not ending, and that his surroundings understand this signal to our partners. He noted that Russian society is increasingly feeling this toxicity, referring to the atmosphere around Putin as very toxic due to long-range missile sanctions. (Source: @UkraineNow/82840)

Russia no longer intends to return part of the occupied territories to Ukraine as part of possible agreements on ending the war, according to sources close to the Kremlin who stated Moscow plans to preserve these territories as buffer zones. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31826)

The Prosecutor General's Office announced the initiation of a public criminal case against Narek Karapetian, leader of the 'Strong Armenia' bloc, for accepting a bribe in the form of five apartments worth over 18 million rubles. (Source: @tass_agency/386527)

The General Prosecutor's Office expanded the opportunities for concluding contracts with the Russian Armed Forces for convicted citizens, including those convicted of smuggling strategically important goods, cultural values, or animals and plants listed in the Red Book of Russia. (Source: @tass_agency/386518)

Russian forces conducted strikes on Ukrainian ports, maritime vessels, and logistics centers involved in the Armed Forces of Ukraine, according to the Ministry of Defense. (Source: @tass_agency/386534)

Maersk announced suspension of operations with one of Ukraine's largest ports due to risks, redirecting a ship with imports destined for the port of Chernomorsk to the Romanian port of Constanta. (Source: @tass_agency/386531)
The US Senate will not transfer $400 million in additional military aid to Ukraine approved by Congress, with funds only available in fiscal year 2029. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31820)

Pentagon head Pete Hegseth stated that the Senate should fund the US armed forces, not Ukraine, calling criticism of financing his own troops with support from Kiev hypocrisy. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31840)

sections.threat_assessment: The Ukrainian military leadership transition from Syrskyi to Drapatyy and Skibiuk represents a significant operational shift that could affect command and control effectiveness during ongoing combat operations. Russian strategic intentions appear to harden regarding occupied territories, with Kremlin sources indicating plans to maintain these areas as buffer zones rather than return them in any peace agreement. Continued Russian strikes on Ukrainian ports and logistics infrastructure, including commercial facilities like Wildberries distribution centers, pose risks to both military supply chains and civilian economic stability. The suspension of operations by major shipping company Maersk at Ukrainian ports due to security risks further degrades critical logistics capabilities. US congressional delays in military aid approval create additional resource constraints for Ukrainian defense operations.
sections.regional_response: European allies continue diplomatic engagement with both Ukrainian and Russian officials, with Zelensky meeting US officials Witkoff and Shubernin to discuss resuming diplomatic efforts, though EU diplomatic efforts failed to agree on an 21st package of anti-Russian sanctions. Belarusian opposition figures in exile face significant challenges accessing education and basic services, with elite figures receiving preferential treatment compared to ordinary emigrants struggling with housing and language training costs. Russian domestic legal actions expanded to allow convicted citizens to enter contracts with the Russian Armed Forces, including those convicted of smuggling strategically important goods. Regional shipping companies are reassessing risk exposure, with Maersk's port suspension reflecting broader industry concerns about operational security in conflict zones.
sections.intelligence_notes: The Ukrainian military leadership transition appears coordinated through presidential decree, with Zelensky emphasizing continuity of command structure despite personnel changes. Russian targeting of logistics infrastructure suggests prioritization of degrading Ukrainian military supply capabilities, though attacks on commercial facilities like Wildberries may represent dual-use targeting or opportunistic strikes. US congressional hold on military aid funding creates uncertainty for Ukrainian operational planning and resource allocation. Intelligence reports indicate Russian forces are maintaining pressure across multiple fronts while simultaneously conducting strategic messaging campaigns through state media outlets. The expansion of Russian legal mechanisms for military recruitment among convicted populations suggests potential manpower challenges and changing force composition strategies.
